errors.english: the first Sanghadisesha
errors.why: dge 'dun gyi lhag ma in a Mūlasarvāstivāda commentary is Sanskrit saṅghāvaśeṣa, not the Pali form.

note: A difficult Vinaya commentary on emission rendered closely; apart from the Pali form of the offense class the reading is defensible.

errors.english: This is the second illustration of the characteristic.
errors.why: Parallel to mtshan nyid gcig pa ('having a single characteristic'), this most likely says the reason here has two characteristics, not that it is a second illustration.

note: Accurate verse rendering of Pātrasvāmin's anyathānupapatti verses, with sound handling of the examples.

errors.english: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: (saṃtāna) the stream of consciousness]
errors.why: The continuum transformed is that of the mantra already produced (by generating successive distinctions in it), not a mental stream of consciousness.

fix.find: transforming the mental continuum [note: original: (saṃtāna) the stream of consciousness]
fix.replace: transforming the continuum [note: original: (saṃtāna), here the series of the mantra itself]

errors.english: It is because one intends to communicate in such a way
errors.why: brda byed pa is the convention-maker (the author of the mantra, as glossed on the previous side), whose intention fixes the result; the English makes it a generic speaker's wish to communicate.

note: Good rendering of the argument on mantras and human intention, but the saṃtāna note misidentifies whose continuum is transformed.

errors.english: Because his words meet with noble beings, they become like a living presence
errors.why: skyes here is 'a gift': when he meets the noble, his words become like a gift; 'living presence' misreads the word and the conditional.

errors.english: The **unfriendly**
errors.why: mi bshes pa is glossed as 'unacquainted, not seen before', i.e. strangers, not hostile people.

errors.english: **He clearly demonstrates the meaning of the logical arguments**
errors.why: As the commentary's own analysis on the next side shows, the verse means 'with very clear reasons he teaches the meanings', not 'the meaning of the arguments'.

note: Readable rendering of a word-by-word verse commentary, with some lexical slips in the glossed verse words.
Faithful rendering of the seed and plant-life pāyattika definitions and the offense classification.

errors.english: In this way, possession [note: Tibetan: (ldan pa), Sanskrit: (saṃyoga), conjunction or contact] is not diverse.
errors.why: ldan pa here is the Vaiśeṣika quality saṃyoga, 'conjunction'; rendering it 'possession' (and earlier 'diverse possessors of blue') throughout obscures the argument that conjunction, being a quality, cannot itself be variegated.

fix.find: In this way, possession [note: Tibetan: (ldan pa), Sanskrit: (saṃyoga), conjunction or contact] is not diverse.
fix.replace: In this way, conjunction [note: Tibetan: (ldan pa), Sanskrit: (saṃyoga)] is not variegated.

note: The argument structure (opponent and reply) is tracked, but saṃyoga is consistently rendered 'possession', which needs correcting throughout.

errors.english: This is not the case; if it possessed parts
errors.why: de lta ma yin te here means 'otherwise': the aggregate must be partless, otherwise, if it had parts, it would not be substantially real; it does not deny the preceding claim.

fix.find: This is not the case; if it possessed parts

errors.english: the meaning of the (Sutra) scriptural discourse
errors.why: mdo here is the root verse of the treatise that the author explains in his own prose, not a Buddhist sūtra.

note: Sound rendering of the argument on atoms and conventional existence, with one connective misread as a denial.

errors.english: Except for those that do not produce filth
errors.why: The subject continues from srog chags at the end of the previous side: except grass in which living creatures do not breed, the rest is to be discarded; 'filth' is not in the text.

fix.find: Except for those that do not produce filth
fix.replace: Except for those in which living creatures do not breed

errors.english: made them establish residences for him
errors.why: gnas 'cha' ba is taking niśraya (dependence) on a teacher: Udāyin had the new monks take dependence on him, which is why they are then called his attendants (nye gnas).

fix.find: made them establish residences for him
fix.replace: had them take dependence (niśraya) on him

errors.english: After Udayin and each of them had received their respective lodgings and sat down
errors.why: The attendants received lodgings for Udāyin and for themselves; Udāyin was outside and did not receive his own lodging, as the next clause makes clear.

errors.english: bundles of grass should be spread out, tied with ropes, and left suspended from trees
errors.why: The bundles of grass meant to be spread on the walking path are to be kept tied and hung on a tree until the time of spreading; they are not spread out and hung at once.

note: The narrative is followable, but several Vinaya details (niśraya, who received lodgings, what is discarded) are misread.

errors.english: the source text from the *Sub-commentary on the Requests* [note: original: "Zhu ba" / Vinayaupayika]
errors.why: zhu ba is the canonical Vinaya 'Questions' (the Upāli questions of the Uttaragrantha), quoted as scripture; it is not a sub-commentary, and the Vinayaupayika identification is wrong.

fix.find: the source text from the *Sub-commentary on the Requests* [note: original: "Zhu ba" / Vinayaupayika]
fix.replace: the source text from the *Questions* [note: original: "Zhu ba", the Vinaya Questions of Upāli]

errors.english: If it is covered with **planks**
errors.why: spang leb are sods/turf slabs; the wooden planks are the following shing leb, which the English renders as 'shingles'.

errors.english: [note: the person responsible for the action leading to a transgression]
errors.why: byed pa po here is the factor that constitutes the offense, which the text itself identifies as the vihāra, not a person.

errors.english: Since there is no specific distinction made, it is understood that the monastery is currently under the authority of the household
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'entirely' is understood because the qualification 'having authority over the house' is NOT stated for the vihāra; the English turns the absent qualification into a positive claim.

note: Structure of question-and-answer is kept, but the scriptural source, building materials and the key notion of byed pa po are misrendered.

span_why: It opens with two sentences from the previous side ('This is because one dedicates it toward the state of Buddhahood itself. One should describe the others in the same way, up to the turning away from wrong views.') before the sentence that crosses the boundary.

errors.english: The (bodhichitta) awakening mind and the compassionate heart of a (bodhisattva) one striving for enlightenment arise
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks only of the bodhisattva's compassionate mind arising; bodhicitta is not mentioned.

errors.english: the absence of intentionality through mere memory
errors.why: This is one of the five purities of morality, 'embraced by mindfulness' (smṛti-parigṛhīta); 'absence of intentionality through mere memory' does not represent the doctrine.

note: Clear rendering of the competing explanations of the hundredfold merit, with one added term and one garbled item in the list of five purities.
